result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_powerlaw_cluster_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a Holme-Kim powerlaw cluster graph: preferential attachment with triangle closing. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_powerlaw_cluster_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a Holme-Kim powerlaw cluster graph: preferential attachment with triangle closing. title: >- [Graph.add_powerlaw_cluster_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add a Holme-Kim powerlaw cluster graph: preferential attachment with triangle closing. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a Holme-Kim powerlaw cluster graph: preferential attachment with triangle closing. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L10297-L10404){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_powerlaw_cluster_graph( n, m, p, seed=None, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Powerlaw cluster graph](../assets/graphs/add-powerlaw-cluster-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three Holme-Kim graphs on a ring of eight nodes, each new node attaching to m=2 others by preferential attachment, with triad-formation probability p=0, 0.5, and 1. Every panel has 12 edges, but a higher p closes more of them into triangles: 1, 4, and 5 triangles." width="100%"} Grows a graph from `m` isolated nodes, adding the other `n - m` nodes one at a time. Each new node makes `m` links. Its first link goes to an existing node chosen with probability proportional to its degree, as in `add_pa_graph()`. For each further link, with probability `p` the new node closes a triangle by linking to a random neighbor of the node it last attached to; otherwise it makes another preferential-attachment link. With `p=0` this is the Barabási-Albert model. Raising `p` raises the clustering, while the degree distribution keeps its power-law tail. The process follows NetworkX's `powerlaw_cluster_graph()`. Each new node normally adds `m` edges, so the graph has close to `(n - m) * m` edges; a few fewer when a triangle-closing link lands on a node the new node was going to attach to anyway. In a directed graph each edge points from the new node to the node it attached to, as in `add_pa_graph()`. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Powerlaw cluster graphs are useful for: - modeling social networks, which combine hubs with many closed triangles - separating the effects of clustering and degree distribution, by sweeping `p=` while the degree distribution stays roughly fixed - benchmarking algorithms on scale-free graphs that aren't locally tree-like ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. Must be at least `m=`. [m]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of links made by each new node. Must be at least `1`. [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of closing a triangle after each link, between `0` and `1`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `m=` is less than `1` or greater than `n=`, or `p=` is not between `0` and `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A hundred nodes, each new one making three links: ::: {#ffb8054c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_powerlaw_cluster_graph(n=100, m=3, p=0.5, seed=2) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (100, 288) ``` ::: ::: Raising `p=` closes more triangles, so the average clustering coefficient climbs: ::: {#9a244f41 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ round( ec.Graph() .add_powerlaw_cluster_graph(n=300, m=3, p=p, seed=2) .average_clustering_coefficient(), 3, ) for p in (0.0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [0.069, 0.219, 0.362, 0.559] ``` ::: :::
